summary: On the seventh day, Walker flew with Plymouth toward a ley-line convergence Elrus had marked, learning that a primal stone stores elemental energy and becomes usable by others only once set in a weapon or wand with a cosmic loom. He wanted night vision, heat detection, and sight through magical darkness worked into his helmet, but Plymouth refused to alter the keystone and warned that forcing more magic into the heat stone without containment would make it implode, so Walker dropped the idea. At the shifted obelisk they found the true convergence about a hundred yards off, Elrus postponed the working for lack of equipment, and his watch showed Walker had already trained for forty-two days. Plymouth’s return rod then dropped them on a mountaintop above the stronghold instead of at the door. Meanwhile the others practiced Gerk’s doorways, spent the night at the tavern, and on the morning of the eighth day took Ord’s fused Staff of the Lantern Bearer and Lantern of Revealing into the woods. Ord’s lost strength was traced to the fight with Gerk’s uncle, the Grunkle, where it became a rune-marked bead that restoration cannot restore because it is hidden rather than gone. The lantern opened ethereal sight; spirits seized the staff, and when Sylan grabbed it the light became a beacon of blackness that vacuumed several spirits into him and blinded Gerk. The last spirits, including an elderly half-elf who named a neighbor, Claire Belle, and a woman begging to reach her son, were released toward New Navel. Dana, Walker, Glimmen, and the larger dragon Araden arrived as the beacon died. Sylan restored Gerk’s sight and said he may have gathered restless souls. The session ended on the edge of Trigash Forest with the spirits unresolved, and with the question of whether Walker’s hat is the lich’s phylactery still open.

plotSections.title: Where the last session left off
bullets: In the cave, Walker talked with Vecna, waited until Vecna left, and kept investigating. He learned what a ley-line convergence is, along with other pieces of his situation.
The rest of the party finished with Carlkin, drank at the pub, and went out to explore the next morning.
Last session's doorway openings were not fixed: size and location can vary with motivation, abilities, and durability, and the openings interact with the surroundings and with each other.
Play resumes at midday on the seventh day. There are two short activity windows before Walker's training in the power chamber.

plotSections.title: Convergence, Nyx, and the gold eagle
bullets: Walker plans to go to the convergence. He settles on calling the site an obelisk after trying pyramid and monolith.
Elrus advised the convergence because it lights up the map. The other lead is Elrus's table in Nyx, to see whether it adds information or holds another gold-eagle marker.
The markers where Elrus was living, in the cave, were generic and not the fancy gold eagle.
Walker flies toward the convergence and picks up Plymouth, who missed the earlier discoveries. Walker is unsure Plymouth has anything further to add.

plotSections.title: Primal stones
bullets: Elrus explains a primal stone: elemental energy poured into a gem and stabilized. Set in a weapon, Walker's fire stone would add fire and magic damage. A worn earring would not do that for a bow; worn, it could only be a focus for Walker's own fire.

Walker may be able to make one himself with a good enough roll and Elrus's help. Ley-line convergences make the work much easier, which is why they are sought after. Capacity scales with the energy spent and with how pure and unflawed the gem is, and forming the stone costs more energy than it stores.

Raw energy stored in gems is safe only for dragonriders, who can draw it in and out through their dragon links. Glimmen, and possibly another dragon such as Rayodin, could use it to a lesser extent. For someone like Plymouth it is an unstable charge: tripping it destroys the vessel and throws magical shrapnel unless the user has heavy magical protection.
A finished primal stone is usable by others only after it is set into a conduit such as a wand or weapon. Handing Gerk the loose stone would not let him cast fire.
Walker's primary element is fire, the first he learned. He can also call water, light, and darkness, and he can already spend energy stored in his gemstones.

Elrus is surprised Walker was not told they had found a convergence. He wants to go back for his equipment, but there is no time: Walker's training is imminent, and Elrus calls him a fledgling. He is still describing how the gems must be cut when Walker steps away.

plotSections.title: Cosmic loom
bullets: Setting a primal stone into an object takes a cosmic loom, a magical containment table that goes by other names. Elrus describes it as an altar with an upside-down table: four pillars, one at each corner, generate a field that holds the energy.

Elrus has tried the working once or twice, needs a loom to do it, and does not know where one is. He could start the carvings and look for pillar materials, but it would take time. Walker does not remember seeing one. Plymouth might be able to set the stones.
A fire primal stone could support fire-based effects, including something defensive. That example is cut off when Walker steps away.

plotSections.title: Doorway practice
bullets: The rest of the party trains while Walker is away. They expect about a day before he returns.

Ciri throws rocks at Gerk while he opens doorways from different directions. Gerk says the day's work is going well and that the Doorman ability seems fine after Sylan pushed him to rein it in. Sylan asks whether Gerk had the ability the whole time.

When training ends, Sylan, Gerk, and the others head for the pub or the keep to find Dana. Gerk says someone there has been adept at sorting out his doorway problems; that person is not named. Sylan hopes Dana has recovered from the visit to Carlkin. She was there for the first part, and Sylan thinks the party sometimes embarrasses her.

plotSections.title: Back at the tavern
bullets: Sylan greets Ciri as if she has just returned. Ciri says she has been with the group the whole time and has not gone anywhere. On royalty, she says she does not know, then that she is still royal, and that she is apparently a very good bar owner. Sylan has not been to the bar often but thinks it is doing well. Ciri tells him not to worry about it.
Dana has been away and is unsure whether she is at the brewery or elsewhere. She chooses to be at the bar.

A map mark for bees is a short, successful hive adventure that supplied the tavern's mead. Sylan remembers a crew of about three and guesses Walker, Ord, or a younger Gerk. The DM says it was Sylan, Patty, and at least one other person.

They arrive while Dana is quietly playing. She waves and keeps playing. Sylan plans a night at the tavern, morning prep, and a meeting with Walker tomorrow, hoping Walker has more information. Gerk has nothing special planned. Sylan intends to talk with Ord about a lantern and a staff, hoping Ord works out how to use them.

plotSections.title: Flight to the obelisk
bullets: Walker's flight is short. He and Plymouth reach a small grassy island where an obelisk stands north of the guild hall. The surroundings are rolling grassy field.

Plymouth asks about a cosmic loom. Walker knows nothing about it. Plymouth calls it a magical item they cannot make, at least not quickly, and says primal stones can be created at the convergence but still need the loom to be set into an item. He bases that on Elrus's account of ley lines.

With the right work, stones can be offensive, defensive, or utility magic, depending on how many are used, how valuable they are, and how they are set. Examples include a blade that flames, burns hot, or both, and a ring or blanket that gives warmth. An item made with Walker's stones could give Gerk fire protection or offensive fire.

Walker wants the work done, but Plymouth says the training matters more. The convergence is a rare, highly magical landmark that would be hard to see again for a very long time, and experiencing it would help Walker's training more than any item he might make there.

plotSections.title: Walker's helmet and the stones on hand
bullets: Walker already has a heat stone, can breathe underwater, and has darkvision. He wants stones set in his helmet: light separated from fire for night vision, heat detection, and a way to see through magical darkness. He will not spend the jewelry he worked hard to make. If the helmet cannot do this, he says the project is not worth doing.

Plymouth says it is possible with time and a very powerful primal stone, but separating light from fire and also detecting heat is complex. Several stones would be easier: one for light, one for heat detection, and possibly a third. A gem of illusion magic, reversed, could help pierce magical darkness, which he describes as an inverse illusion or an absence of light.
Plymouth has no gems or diamonds. He forgot most of his equipment, bought only odds and ends in Sunder, and is carrying powdered dragon liver.

Walker shows his heat stone and keystone and asks whether an item that already has a magical property can take more magic. Plymouth refuses any experiment on the keystone. In a free, unbound state, added magic would be highly unstable, would take a great deal of energy to contain, and could damage the caster or the item; an item that cannot hold the energy will simply fail.

The heat stone only keeps its bearer warm. Plymouth says more fire magic might go into it, then rolls it over, pinches it lengthwise, and hands it back. It works as advertised, but without proper containment any added energy would make it implode immediately. Walker drops the idea.

plotSections.title: Nyx Cage and the heat stones
bullets: The warming stones were bought in Agenheim because it was cold, in one of the -heim lands, on the way toward Jotunheim and the seeing stones.

The seller was Nyx Cage the Ice Mage. He offered a discount if the party went to Helheim and stole a peace treaty between the people of Helheim, described as goliaths, and the giants. They remember the offer and did not take it.
No one had kept his name until the DM supplied it. Walker allows that Nyx Cage could be an alias. Plymouth finds the name shady and does not know him.

plotSections.title: The shifted obelisk
bullets: The party is already at the obelisk. It has no base. It sits on bare ground, slightly angled and slightly embedded, with grass growing around it. The ground feels no different from the surrounding field.

Walker had said the obelisk was shifted off the ley line. His notes and drawings are gone. He remembers the mountain to the west, the obelisk to the north, and a shift of about twenty degrees from the center.

They have traveled about 5.6 miles. Facing back toward the guild, the true ley-line point is to the right of the obelisk, about a hundred yards. Walker treats the twenty-degree figure as far too large.

plotSections.title: Elrus postpones the working
bullets: Walker asks whether they must meditate for the working to succeed. Elrus says meditation is not required, but they should meditate anyway.
Elrus tries a simple cantrip from pocket scraps: a small pebble, scorched moss, and an insect. Light shines brightly out to about sixty feet and continues another sixty feet beyond that.

Elrus is not properly equipped and wants everyone to leave and return later. Walker agrees and plans to gather more stones and more energy. They agree to meditate, train, do more magic training on site, and return to Midgard before trying again.

plotSections.title: Forty-two days and the return rod
bullets: Walker thinks only about two weeks have passed for him. Elrus checks a watch and says it has been exactly forty-two days, and that Walker has been training the entire time even while being told he still needs to train more.

Walker pins the site for later: from the tower, 0.01 radians to the west, his right when facing the guild, then 5.6 miles. An earlier wording of two miles northwest is corrected to that heading and distance.

Walker will not imbue primal stones yet. He wants the party's input first. He floats night vision for himself and, less certainly, a bard instrument that would strengthen Dana's magic, and says the cosmic loom still has to be figured out before he knows how useful a stone would be.

Plymouth takes a collapsible rod from a telescope-like case on his belt. It is about a foot long, with adjustment knobs, and one end is a broad, rounded, three-pronged head. He sets it for the convergence and the 5.6-mile distance, plants it, and tells everyone to stand close. Electrical energy arcs around it, then a lightning crack and flash carry the group away.

They arrive on a brisk mountaintop overlooking a valley, not on the grassy island. Plymouth recovers the smoldering rod and says he was a little off: a little farther and it would have been quite bad. He had been aiming for the stronghold's front door. By his calculations the stronghold is down in the valley. Walker thanks him.

plotSections.title: Morning of the eighth day
bullets: For the group at the stronghold it is the morning of the eighth day. They have had no contact from Walker. The morning is brisk, fall is coming in, and thunder and lightning roll in the distance.

Sylan has been up a couple of hours and has been working with Gerk. He checks on Ord. Ord asks for help with his lantern. They plan to work outside in the woods, away from people, for about an hour, because a similar outing worked last time. Sylan has an ability ready so they do not blind themselves.
Ord found the lantern in Volga. Sylan found a staff at Shades and Trades and thought the two belonged together.

plotSections.title: Ord's missing strength
bullets: Ord has been trying to regain his lost strength and has made no progress. He does not think the loss came from his duel with Gerk. As he first remembers it, they were at a place heard as "the orc Tam," his strength went into a little object heard as "a little Ord," and someone else touched it instead of him. He also says he cannot see.

The clearer account is the fight with Gerk's uncle, the Grunkle, which ended with the uncle dying after he had taken some of Ord's strength. Sylan first remembered the uncle punching the strength out of Gerk. A floating Ord then appeared and solidified into a runic bead, or a sphere with a rune on it. Dana was involved as it solidified.

Dana could not fix it. Restoration, greater restoration, and everything else she has were already tried. The clue still holds: you cannot restore what is not missing, so the strength is hidden rather than gone.
Sylan suggests a monk might explain what the fight did. Ord thinks that is worth pursuing later and wants to deal with the lantern first.

plotSections.title: Who lives in the keep
bullets: Sylan asks for a roster. He thinks about twenty people live in the keep and does not know their names. The roster is on a different map than the one at hand.
Mahali is there and earns his place by cooking.

Their secrets man, remembered as the rat, is missing, treated as an unscheduled vacation. Sylan thought he had taken leave without asking. The party needs to remember where they left him. They had chosen him for his resourcefulness.

A small white monkey may be a monk or only a special fighter. Ord treats that figure as the little one and asks for the father's name, almost calling him Benji. The name on the notes is Koji. Sylan does not remember spending time with Koji.
A little gold person who makes something gold is Ord's roommate. The name came through as Banshee, then Archie, and the table settled on Ponchi.

plotSections.title: The fused lantern-staff
bullets: Ord and Sylan take the lantern-staff to their usual door-testing spot in the woods to speak its inscription again. Ord remembers the words but does not have them written down. The DM does not have the original inscription either and treats the wording as deep lore still to be workshopped.

The components are a Staff of the Lantern Bearer, which Sylan remembered as the Staff of the Lantern Keeper, and a Lantern of Revealing. The lantern's name was misremembered as "lantern of the staff keeper." The two were already drawn together, and they fused in an earlier impromptu working when the lantern's inscription was read. Sylan asks whether they could still be tried separately; the DM confirms they are fused, and Sylan treats that as having been part of the plan.

The lantern is hooded and finely made. Detect Magic showed an aura of evocation. It has two settings, and one of them blinded an entire room. Saying the words made something happen; trying to undo it made something else happen, and the effect was hard to dismiss. Ord is using a shield, so a sword plus this lantern is the working picture.

The DM says the lantern was identified at Shades and Trades. On November 3, campaign year 25, Ord experimented with it, saw into the Ethereal Plane, and blinded himself until Sylan cured him with lesser restoration. No spirits were present that time. The result was set aside because the previous session ended with an emissary arriving with a finger in a box.

This time Ord offers an improvised phrase, "Brightest day in darkness," and a working oath that no evil shall escape his sight and that those who worship evil should beware his power, then calls the lantern's light. The DM treats those words as still being workshopped.

plotSections.title: The white dragon's hoard
bullets: The lantern and staff come from the white dragon's hoard. The DM's notes date that treasure to November 3 of the previous year. Dana still has the inventory. She did not write down most of the magic items because the broom she received is the one she tracked.

Counted wealth: about two dozen gemstones, art objects, mundane goods, 500 platinum, 60,000 gold, 11,000 silver, and 4,100 copper. Sylan remembers four or five magic items. Dana personally received a magic broom and a set of bone dice.

Other pieces Dana lists: a small shrine with a statuette, a brazier, and an altar to a god of dragon minions; a scroll with a poem; the skull of a fiend or celestial; seven candlesticks marked with a holy symbol; a gold bracelet; a gold locket with a painted portrait; a copper chalice; and two carved bone statuettes.

Sylan gave the gold birdcage from that hoard to the crew. A box of turquoise animal figurines was also in the hoard. Ord inspected them and left them behind, and Sylan suspects they might turn into creatures.

A separate hoard item, a ring or bracelet, went to Ciri. It shoots starbursts that turn into fireballs. Guesses at the name include Nightfall and Starfall. Nobody present remembers the real name, and Ciri is away.

Dana identifies the undead woman tied to the hoard as Lady Meriwether, a name the table connects to Merryweather from Sleeping Beauty. The white dragon's own name is not recovered. Sylan's line that the name is "Lost of Time" reads as the dragon's name being lost to time.

plotSections.title: Walker's hat and the phylactery
bullets: Sylan wants the party, once Walker is back, to test whether the hat Walker has been wearing is the lich's phylactery, and to decide whether to do that in the open or in secret. Dana is already comparing her notes and books to a Legend Lore vision on that question.

Sylan worries the lich can simply make another phylactery and shrug the loss off. Dana's plan is to destroy the phylactery and kill the lich before he can form a new one. Sylan expects that holding the soul would make the lich easier to find, and Dana agrees that is a fair assumption.

Sylan flags two conditions: the hat must actually be a phylactery, and wearing it must not have corrupted Walker. He remembers the first time Walker put it on as questionable. Walker, once back, brushes it off with "Wouldn't you like to know?"

plotSections.title: Ethereal sight in the woods
bullets: Ord and Sylan are in a wooded strip at the secret door-testing grounds, away from the stronghold. Sylan looks away and closes his eyes. Ord closes his eyes as well, because the last activation blinded him.
Gerk is in a shady spot within thirty feet, watching rather than taking part. Dana is in her tower with her broom ready; she knows which way they went and is deep in her books. Ciri is gone.

The forest flashes. For Ord the activation is also an audible tone. He sees the world in grayscale, semi-opaque and ghostly: the Ethereal Plane, with shadows moving through the woods that were not visible before. The lantern burns a desaturated blue, and Ord's eyes match it: flat color, no pupils, with a little smoke when he blinks.
Sylan appears several shades darker than the surroundings. About half a dozen cloudy, semi-translucent figures mill around him, half above him and half passing through him.

Ord tells Sylan what he sees, wonders whether the sight pierces magical darkness, and slowly brings the staff toward the nearest figure. The being startles, looks from the lantern to Ord, and grabs the crook, trying to wrench it away. Its face is gaunt, its eyes crazed, and its body is only half solid, but it can grip the staff.

Ord holds on and asks whether it can hear him and who it is. A wail answers inside his head. As the being screams, its edges fray and dematerialize like burning paper. The other five turn, howl, and move toward the lantern. Three or four are soon pulling on it, and the first is about half burnt away. Sylan only sees the staff jerk and asks if Ord is all right.

plotSections.title: The black beacon and the return
bullets: Gerk looked at the light and fails a Wisdom save: 3 on the die, plus 5 from within thirty feet of Ord's ward, for a total of 8 against a DC that needs to break 10. He is blinded, fumbling on the ground, screaming, and whirling his hammer overhead to keep things off him. He is not moving to strike.

Sylan grabs the staff to wrench it back toward Ord. They expect the same blinding flash as last time and are curious whether the sight transfers. When Sylan's hand closes on the active staff, the lantern's light becomes incandescent shadow, a roiling ball of shadow glowing inside it. The translucent spirits erupt outward and drop around Ord and Sylan as incomplete physical bodies. The air crackles, and the glade is both the darkest and the brightest it has been.

From the stronghold that moment is a beacon of eternal blackness rising from the treeline: a swirling mass of ink with a shadowy wave that can be felt passing through everything. Dana calls it a giant pillar of darkness and leaves the tower on her broom, which flies 50 feet. She expects to need a couple of turns to arrive.

Walker had meant to set Plymouth Gawater down and then go to Grazog. Plymouth asks to be left at New Navel and says he will make his own way; the party still badly needs to talk to him. Glimmen and Araden, a dragon several sizes larger than Glimmen, land near the stronghold. The village, used to Glimmen alone, buzzes at the second dragon. Plymouth scrambles off and heads for New Navel. One or two gatehouse guards hail Walker.

Walker and Dana see the beacon. Walker tells Elrus there is a change of plans: they had been going to train rather than continue to Grazog. Elrus takes the disturbance as the companions, Araden is cited as agreeing, and Walker and Elrus take off after Dana. Glimmen overtakes the broom.

In the air, Dana says it is nice of them to show up. Walker asks what is happening. Dana guesses the others are messing with a magical item. She says she was indisposed for a couple of days and that this is what happens when she and Walker are both gone. Walker's line about being gone forty-nine days is a joke he immediately walks back. Sylan calls the scene a literal dark age.

plotSections.title: Spirits pulled into Sylan
bullets: This use of the staff has not been shut off. Toasting the spirits while the ethereal sight is active is what draws them in. Once a spirit comes within about four feet of Sylan while he holds the active staff, a vortex sucks it into him. He feels no change. The pull is a byproduct of touching the staff while it is active. Blind Gerk only hears the sucking and yells that he cannot see.

Sylan does not recognize the figures. They look much alike except one fitter spirit whose defining mark is a large wound down the center of his face, a killing blow. After being pulled in, the remaining spirits crawl the other way and cannot break the pull.

Four spirits are taken, leaving two. Absorbed spirits look less blue-ethereal and more shaded black, and they read as light-producing. The two still outside are shaded black and are no longer light-producing.

Sylan keeps hold. He has dealt with spirits before, did not expect them to follow him, says he did not purge anyone, and believes they followed for a reason. He wants to see it through and asks Ord whether to let go.
Ord suggests saying the incantation backwards to turn the effect off. He notes that the last time they tried to shut it off, something else happened. The backward attempt is not carried through.

plotSections.title: Ledzbika and the last spirit
bullets: Ord keeps one hand on the staff and grapples one of the last two spirits. It is half-formed but solid enough to hold, like a ghost given physical form, and it still functions in that half-life. It has been brought from the Ethereal onto the material. A magical pull drags it toward Sylan, and Ord's grip is the only thing keeping it back.

Ord uses Divine Sense while holding the staff and the spirit, and the DM has him swirl them as part of the cast. Strong evil registers as a noxious odor. Until the end of his next turn he knows the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead in range, and the type, but not a finer subtype. These are undead: spectral spirits made physical. Ord has used Divine Sense once before, in Volga.

The held spirit is an elderly half-elf. He says they have disturbed his peace, demands release, and gives his name as Ledzbika. When asked again he says he already gave it, and the table also hears Bannaby, Burton, Barnaby, and Carnaby. Sylan hears him. He calls Sylan a fiend, says he is not trying to reach Sylan, and says he is trying to return to his abode. He says the one who shed the light burned them and that Sylan is sucking the rest of them in.

He says the woman next door, Claire Belle, stole from him and his family, that his silver is under the floorboards, and that this is why his children are starving. He calls her a conniving liar and says he is stuck and must get back to find her. Asked where his abode is, he does not give a place. He also says the party pulled them from life. Sylan asks whether these ghosts are from Morgan. That is not answered.
A separate raspy voice also demands to be let go, calls them fiends, says they stole from him, and says he was pulled from his floorboards as the party walked by today. It is not named.

Sylan says he may be able to talk to them again if Ord lets this one go, and that they should settle this first. Ord releases him. As he dematerializes he reaches toward New Navel. The words that go with the gesture are lost. He snaps away. The last spirit clings to a root while being pulled.

Ord grabs the last spirit: an amorphous upper body of an elderly, sickly, pockmarked woman. Unlike the earlier spirits, she death-grips his hand and begs him not to let go. It is not her time, her son does not know and needs to know, and the darkness is pulling her. She never gives her name or her son's, only repeating "my son" and "my name."

Ord offers to carry a message. They decide they are getting nowhere, and Ord lets her go. While he holds her she can grip him; the moment he chooses to release her, her hands dematerialize, pass through him, and she is vacuumed away. The area goes oddly quiet. Sylan and Ord take these figures for spirits from Old Navel, stirred up as the party passed. Sylan suspects this one is not giving a usable story and jokes that it is like a ghost retirement home.

plotSections.title: The beacon dies
bullets: While Sylan and Ord still have their hands together on the staff, the black beacon keeps erupting from the joined hands. Sylan compares it to Call of Cthulhu and lets go after Ord tells him he can.

When the staff is released, the clearing dies in light. Dana and Walker see the beacon vanish, leaving only a brief afterimage. No more spirits close in. At about sixty feet, hands and silhouettes still flash in and out of the forest edge, but they do not approach.
Ord can still see in an almost wireframe style. He turns the sight off by intent. A long blink extinguishes it, and the forest looks ordinary again.

plotSections.title: Blind Gerk and the reunion
bullets: Gerk is still blind and refuses to stop swinging the hammer. He is terrified, cannot see, and says his eyes are all he has. Tremorsense tells him something is approaching. Sylan says it is a friend. Gerk fears a mimic and demands proof.

Walker jokes that Sylan should claim to be Gerk's dad, a joke only Gerk would know. Sylan will not use that and does not think Gerk will remember their call phrases. The phrase they land on is "I don't trust the cat man," which Gerk says is the one note he has written down and which Sylan confirms is the first. Walker also throws out "scoop fruit" and "loincloth."

Flapping becomes audible as Glimmen and Araden arrive. Gerk asks to touch Sylan's face, keeps the hammer raised, and reaches out ready to strike. Sylan casts lesser restoration through the touch. Gerk's sight returns, he recognizes Sylan, and he picks him up.

Sylan says the staff test left him with problems in New Navel. He thinks he picked up restless souls and may need a couple of days there as a ghost detective, possibly at Carlkin's house, now that Walker is back. He says he thought the little girl might be alone and kept extra spirits so she would have company. Gerk, who has dealt with voices in his head before, panics at being haunted and drops Sylan.

Dana and Walker arrive as the two dragons land beside the forest. Dana scolds Ord, calling him Lord Bronztail, and tells Sylan not to touch magical items that are not his. Gerk insists Sylan haunted him.

plotSections.title: End of session
bullets: The party is together again on the outskirts of Trigash Forest.

The DM recap: Ord opened a third eye with the lantern, the staff work drew spooky magic, and the spirits were mixed. Some would not leave, and some seemed to be trying to get back to neighbors. What that means is left for next session.

log: The DM recaps the cave: Walker spoke with Vecna, waited for him to leave, investigated further, and learned what a ley-line convergence is. The other party members finished with Carlkin, spent a night drinking at the pub, and set out to explore the next morning.
The DM recaps that openings could be made at different sizes and locations depending on motivation, abilities, and durability, and that they interact with the surroundings and each other.
It is midday on the seventh day, with two activity windows left before Walker's training montage.

Walker chooses the convergence obelisk. Elrus recommended it because it lights up the map, and Walker also wants to check Elrus's table in Nyx for more information or another gold eagle. The cave where Elrus was living had only generic markers, not a gold eagle.

Flying toward the convergence with Plymouth aboard, Walker confirms primal stones: fire energy imbued into a stone, then set in a sword, yields fire and magic damage. Convergences make that crafting much easier, possibly doable by Walker himself with Elrus's help. Walker establishes fire as his primary element and says he can already call fire, water, light, darkness, and the energy in his gemstones, and asks what a primal stone adds if he can already call elements and spend energy stored in gems, including what a fire earring on his bow would do.

Elrus explains that dragonriders can safely use that raw stored energy, that primal stones stabilize it for other users once set in a conduit, and that gem quality and energy spent set the stone's strength. Gerk could not cast from a loose stone. Setting the stone takes a cosmic loom, which Elrus does not currently know how to find, though he could try to build one over time. He starts a fire-stone example that includes a defensive use.

The instructor has just learned of the ley-line convergence, has no equipment on hand, and cannot delay Walker's imminent training to fetch it. Walker does not remember a cosmic loom. The instructor offers to start pillar carvings later and begins detailing gem cuts, then Walker steps away.
Meanwhile Gerk practices opening doorways from different directions while Ciri throws rocks at him. Gerk says the Doorman training seems fine. Sylan asks if Gerk had the ability the whole time.

Sylan assumes Ciri has returned from a journey. Ciri says she never left, is still royal, that her royalty situation is complicated, and that she is a successful bar owner. Sylan says the bar seems to be doing well.
Dana notices the bees mark. Sylan and the DM tie it to a one-session hive run that supplies the tavern's mead. The DM identifies Sylan and Patty among that short crew.

Dana does not know where her character is and places herself at the bar. The others finish training and travel back to meet her at the pub or the keep. Sylan asks whether she has recovered from the visit to Carlkin.

The party reaches the tavern while Dana is playing. They plan to spend the rest of the day there, stay the night, prepare in the morning, and see Walker tomorrow. Sylan plans to ask Ord about the lantern and staff Sylan gave him.

Walker and Plymouth finish a short flight and land on an island with an obelisk north of the guild hall. Plymouth explains that primal stones, once set with a cosmic loom, can provide fire protection, offensive fire, or utility such as warmth, according to the number, value, and setting of the stones. Walker remains undecided about them.

Walker proposes imbuing his helmet for night vision, heat vision, and sight through magical darkness without using his personal jewelry. Plymouth says it is possible but complex and easier with multiple powerful stones, and that a cosmic loom is required. He says the convergence is a rare, highly magical landmark worth the trip because it will help Walker's training. Plymouth has no spare gems, only Sunder odds and ends and powdered dragon liver.

Walker shows a heat stone and a keystone and asks if more magic can be added to a stone that is already magical. Plymouth forbids altering the keystone, says the heat stone might accept more fire magic, and warns that forcing more magic in without containment, especially in a free state, is unstable and can implode, destroying the caster or the item. Walker abandons the plan.

The party recalls the heat stones were bought in Agenheim from Nyx Cage the Ice Mage, who gave Walker the item and wanted them to steal a Helheim goliath–giant peace treaty for a discount. They never did the job.

At the obelisk, Walker reconstructs the ley-line offset from notes and memory: mountain west, obelisk north, about twenty degrees off center, drawings gone, after roughly 5.6 miles of travel. The corrected point is about a hundred yards to the right of the obelisk when facing the guild. The spot feels like ordinary rolling grass. The obelisk sits angled on bare ground with no base.

Elrus says meditation is not required for the working but should be done anyway, then casts an under-equipped cantrip with a pebble, scorched moss, and an insect, lighting roughly sixty feet plus another sixty. He calls off the real attempt until he has proper equipment. Walker agrees to gather more stones and energy. They agree to train and return to Midgard.

Elrus's watch reads exactly forty-two days. Walker had felt about two weeks and had not registered the training. He pins the return route from the tower as 0.01 radians west, then 5.6 miles, and declines to imbue primal stones until he talks with the party, citing night vision, Dana, and the cosmic loom.

Plymouth plants his foot-long adjustable rod after accounting for convergence and distance, and the group is told to stand close. Walker agrees. Energy arcs around the rod and lightning transports them from the grassy knoll to a brisk mountaintop above the stronghold rather than the front door. Plymouth recovers the smoldering rod, stows it, and admits the landing was off.
The view switches to the others on the morning of the eighth day. They still have had no in-game word from Walker. The morning is brisk, fall is arriving, and thunder sounds in the distance.

Sylan, after working with Gerk, checks on Ord. They agree to experiment outside in the woods, away from people, with Ord's Volga lantern and the staff Sylan found at Shades and Trades, possibly fusing them, without blinding themselves. The DM later confirms the two items are fused: the Staff of the Lantern Bearer (also called the Staff of the Lantern Keeper) and the Lantern of Revealing. The paired lantern's separate name and whether the two can still be separated stay unresolved.

Ord says his strength still has not returned and that he can't see. He traces the loss to the fight with Gerk's uncle, the Grunkle, who died after taking some of that strength; it became a floating form and then a rune-marked bead or sphere, not to the duel with Gerk. Restoration, including Dana's and greater restoration, failed because the strength is hidden in Gerk rather than missing.
Sylan suggests finding a monk who might explain the fight. Ord wants to start with the lantern, and the party turns to the staff.

They try to name the keep's residents. Mahali is the cook. Their secrets man is regarded as away without leave, and the DM presses them to remember where they left him. The roster name Koji is confused with Benji and with a little white monkey who may be a monk or a fighter; Sylan does not remember Koji being among them, and Koji is placed as father of that monkey. Ord describes a small gold person who makes something gold; the DM identifies Ord's roommate, and Ord names him Ponchi.

Dana reads her notes from the white dragon's hoard, dated in the DM's notes to November 3 of the previous year: her broom and bone dice, two carved bone statuettes, a gold bracelet, a gold locket with a painted portrait, a copper chalice, gemstones, 500 platinum, 60,000 gold, 11,000 silver, 4,100 copper, a shrine to a god of dragon minions, and the gold birdcage Sylan gave the crew. The DM adds a box of turquoise animal figurines, which Ord inspected and left behind; Sylan thinks they may become creatures. Sylan guesses the associated name is Lost of Time. Dana names the undead woman Lady Meriwether.
Dana says Ciri holds the ring or bracelet that fires starbursts which become fireballs. Ciri is absent, and the name (Nightfall, Starfall, or similar) is not recovered.

Ord recalls the hooded lantern: finely made, an aura of evocation, two settings, one of which blinded a whole room, and a command effect that was difficult to end. Sylan remembers not to look at it when it goes off. The DM places the identification at Shades and Trades. The inscription is missing from the notes. The November 3, 2025 experiment let Ord see the Ethereal Plane and was immediately overshadowed by an emissary bringing a finger in a box. Ord supplies "Brightest day in darkness" as an ignition phrase; the DM sets the real incantation aside to workshop later.

Sylan proposes checking whether Walker's hat is a phylactery, in daylight or in secret, and whether it has corrupted him. Dana says the phylactery must be destroyed and the lich killed before a new one is made. Sylan hopes possessing the soul would help locate him. Walker, asked about that corruption, does not answer directly and says "Wouldn't you like to know?"

In the woods at the door-testing grounds, away from the others, Ord activates the fused staff and lantern. Sylan looks away. Ord closes his eyes, having gone blind the last time, and recites a paladin-style charge over the staff lantern.

The forest flashes. Ord perceives the Ethereal Plane in ghostly grayscale. Shadows move in the woods. His eyes and the lantern glow desaturated blue. Sylan shows darker than the ghostly surroundings, with about six cloudy figures drifting around and through him.

Ord extends the staff toward the nearest figure. It grabs the crook and tries to pull the lantern free. Its face is gaunt and its form only half solid. Ord asks who it is. A wail sounds inside his head. The figure's edges burn away, and the other five howl and advance on the lantern.

Sylan grabs the staff and wrenches it back toward Ord. Three or four spirits are on it and the first is about half gone. The lantern jerks in Ord's hand. It turns to incandescent shadow, the spirits fall as unfinished physical forms, and a beacon of blackness erupts from the treeline.

Spirits within about four feet of Sylan are vacuumed into him. He feels nothing, recognizes none of them, and keeps holding the staff. One has a killing wound down the center of his face. The rest crawl against the pull and cannot escape. Dana sees the pillar of darkness from her tower and flies her broom toward it. Gerk, within thirty feet and having looked at the light, fails a Wisdom save (a 7, also given as 3 + 5 = 8), is left blind on the ground, and can hear the vacuum but not see it. Ciri is gone.

Another spirit is sucked in while Sylan chooses not to release the staff. Ord starts speaking the incantation backwards. The DM says this use was never shut off, and recalls that Ord's earlier use, placed by the table in Volga, showed him the Ethereal and blinded him until lesser restoration. The remaining spirits look shaded black rather than blue ethereal. Four are gone and two remain.

Ord holds the staff and grapples one remaining spirit, pinning a now-physical elderly half-elf against the pull toward Sylan. The spirit demands to be released, says they have disturbed his peace, that he must return and is not trying to reach Sylan, that the woman next door stole his silver from under the floorboards and left his children starving, and that the one who shed light on them burned them. He names Claire Belle as that neighbor and says he already gave his name; the party does not cleanly catch it, including a rendering like Ledzbika. Sylan asks if the ghosts are from Morgan and gets no answer. A separate raspy voice also demands freedom, calls them fiends, says he was pulled from his floorboards as they walked by, and that their friend is sucking the spirits in.
Ord uses Divine Sense. The spirits register as undead, spectral spirits made physical, type only and no subtype. Strong evil smells noxious.

Sylan begins to offer that he might be able to do something, then tells Ord to let the held spirit go so they can settle this and maybe speak to them again. Ord releases him. The spirit dematerializes, reaching toward New Navel, and snaps away. The last spirit clings to a root while being pulled.

Gerk sits screaming and whirling his hammer. Dana is already flying from the tower toward the beacon of celestial darkness. Walker, back from mountainside training with Glimmen and the much larger Araden, had planned to drop Plymouth Gawater at New Navel and then go to Grazog. Plymouth walks off toward New Navel on his own. Dana, who had been researching whether the helmet is the phylactery, sees the dragons land; the village reacts and gatehouse guards hail Walker. Walker tells Elrus the plan has changed. They leave the Grazog errand and fly after Dana. Glimmen overtakes her broom.
Dana tells Walker she thinks the others are using a magical item and that things went wrong while she and Walker were away. Glimmen and Araden match pace with the party over the large dark vortex.

Sylan agrees they are not getting anywhere and says something has gone wrong. Ord grabs the last spirit, a sickly elderly woman. She begs him to hold on so she can tell her son something before the darkness takes her, but she gives no name and no clear message.

Ord releases her. She loses physical purchase and is vacuumed away, and the area goes quiet. Spirits no longer approach. A black luminescent beacon from the hands on the staff pours into the sky. Sylan lets go and the beacon dies, with a brief afterimage for Dana and Walker. Silhouettes and hands still flicker about sixty feet out at the forest edge.
Ord wills the wireframe spirit-sight off with a long blink and can see the forest normally again.

Sylan approaches blind, hammer-swinging Gerk. Gerk's tremorsense picks up someone approaching; he suspects a mimic and will not trust it. They use the written call phrase "I don't trust the cat man," which Sylan confirms. Wingbeats arrive. Gerk holds the hammer ready and reaches to touch Sylan's face. Sylan casts lesser restoration. Gerk can see and recognizes him.

Sylan explains the staff test and says he may have gathered restless souls, including company for the little girl, and may have to do ghost-detective work in New Navel at Carlkin's. Gerk panics about being haunted. Dana and Walker land on the two dragons and Dana scolds Ord and Sylan.
Session ends on the outskirts of Trigash Forest, with the beacon and the spirits unresolved.
